audience: Research contributors, product teams and prospective funders for a named product program.
problem: Research funding and attribution can be opaque: a token balance alone does not show what was researched, what is novel, who contributed, or whether any result was valid.
value_proposition: A versioned research and contribution record lets participants inspect the question, baseline, evidence, credit and proposed economics before committing resources.
value_mechanism: Bind program disclosure, source-relative novelty, controlled research evidence, challengeable attribution and separate economic decisions.
first_order_principles: A claim is limited by its evidence and comparison scope.
Execution work and durable research advance are different.
Rights and payment require explicit agreements and owner decisions.

intended_outcomes.statement: Independent reviewers can reproduce a novelty disposition and identify unresolved checks.
A contributor can trace a proposed award to one accepted work or research-advance assessment.

assumptions: Contributors will use disclosure records when deciding whether to work or fund.
Independent review can identify operative novelty more reliably than self-rating.
A legally workable contribution and revenue contract can be designed.

hypotheses.statement: Independent blind review reduces duplicate or surface-variant awards relative to unreviewed submission.
A replayable attribution procedure yields more stable credit than unstructured owner discretion.

boundaries: No scientific priority claim from local novelty.
No issued token, enforceable return, product validation or personal-data access.
revision_criteria: Pilot reviewers cannot reproduce the novelty distinctions.
Attribution is unstable under blind replay.
Rights or revenue terms cannot be defined without unfair or unenforceable promises.
